title: Expected Return Causes Outcome-Level Mode Collapse in Reinforcement Learning and How to Fix It with Inverse Probability Scaling
abstract: arXiv:2601.21669v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Many reinforcement learning (RL) problems admit multiple terminal solutions of comparable quality, where the goal is not to identify a single optimum but to represent a diverse set of high-quality outcomes. Nevertheless, policies trained by standard expected return maximization routinely collapse onto a small subset of outcomes, a phenomenon commonly attributed to insufficient exploration or weak regularization. We show that this explanation is incomplete: outcome level mode collapse is a structural consequence of the expected-return objective itself. translated_title: 期望回报导致强化学习中结果层面的模式坍缩，以及如何用逆概率缩放来修复它
translated_abstract: 许多强化学习（RL）问题存在多个质量相当的终端解决方案，其目标不是找到单一最优解，而是表示一组多样化的高质量结果。然而，通过标准期望回报最大化训练出的策略往往会坍缩到一小部分结果上，这一现象通常被归因于探索不足或正则化不足。我们证明这一解释是不完整的：结果层面的模式坍缩是期望回报目标本身的结构性必然结果。在理想化的学习动力学下，任意两个结果之间的对数概率比会随其奖励差线性演化，这意味着概率比将呈指数级发散，且无论采用何种探索策略、熵正则化或优化算法，坍缩都不可避免。我们将这一病态的根源确认为期望内部的概率乘数……
tldr: 该论文证明强化学习中结果层面的模式坍缩并非源于探索或正则化不足，而是期望回报目标本身的结构性必然结果，并提出用逆概率缩放的方法来修复这一问题。
en_tdlr: This paper proves that outcome-level mode collapse in reinforcement learning is a structural consequence of the expected-return objective itself—inevitable regardless of exploration or regularization—and proposes inverse probability scaling as a fix.
